hero.title: Robotics that serves those who served.
hero.subtitle: We run hands-on robotics sessions for veterans at the Milwaukee VA, building right alongside them. What started as a one-off series became an ongoing partnership — we're the only team they've asked back.

impact.label: Why it matters
impact.text: The Milwaukee VA keeps inviting us back — no other robotics team has gotten a second invite. Veterans and their families now show up to volunteer and cheer at our Rookie Qualifier, too. It's become a two-way thing.

stats.label: Programs
stats.hint: From intro robotics to advanced builds

approach.label: Our Approach
approach.heading: Build-first. One-on-one. No experience needed.
approach.body:
The program leans on therapeutic recreation — hands-on activity as healing. Every session is build-first: hardware in hand within five minutes, no lectures, and a one-on-one GEarheads mentor so nobody's waiting around.

Mentors are close in age to junior veterans, so it feels like two people solving a problem, not teacher and student. Skeptics relax once they see the real goal is just to build something that works — and FLL/SPIKE makes that easy, since a failed build tells you exactly what to fix.

Skills stack across the two six-week series instead of resetting each week. By the CAD/CNC program in series two, veterans are applying design thinking that started with LEGO motors — the same progression we use for our own new members.

inlinePhoto.caption: GEarheads mentor working one-on-one with a veteran on a SPIKE Prime build

activities.label: FLL
activities.heading: Starting With FLL
activities.text: Every series opens with FIRST LEGO League — veterans build a LEGO robot and program it to run missions on a themed field. No experience needed; a mentor works one-on-one with each person, and every session ends with something that works. Returning veterans move up to SPIKE Prime.

photo.caption: Veteran building a LEGO robot during an intro FLL session

activities.label: CNC
activities.heading: From Screen To Sign
activities.text: The second series goes from screen to shop floor: veterans learn CAD basics, design a custom sign, then watch it get cut on a real CNC machine. Everyone leaves with a finished piece they made themselves.

photo.caption: CNC sign reveal — a finished personalized piece

activities.label: Model Rockets
activities.heading: What's Next: Model Rockets
activities.text: Next up, we're taking the same build-first approach into aerospace — building and launching model rockets.

photo.caption: Reserved for the first model rocket launch with the group

howItRuns.label: Six-Week Series
howItRuns.desc: Two six-week series each season — one intro, one advanced. Skills carry forward week to week, so it feels like real progress, not a string of one-offs.

howItRuns.label: Weekly Sessions
howItRuns.desc: Twelve sessions total, about 90 minutes each. Same day, same time, same mentors every week — that consistency matters as much as the content.

howItRuns.label: Hands-On
howItRuns.desc: Hardware's in hand within the first few minutes — no slide decks, no lectures. Mentors work one-on-one the whole session, whether that's a build step or a line of code.
